plw_a_look_at_stratholme.description:
I'm Eligor Dawnbringer, and I command the Argent Dawn here. I haven't seen Stratholme since it fell. I won't send the Dawn in until somebody I trust has looked at it and come back.

I'm asking you to be that somebody. Walk to the city's gate and look at it, nothing more. Then come back and tell me.

Go west along the road, north past the Fungal Vale, and west through Plaguewood. The gate's at the end of it. Don't go in, whatever you hear.
plw_a_look_at_stratholme.accept_text: Go at midday, when the light's best. I'd like you to see it clearly.

plw_carrion_grubs.description:
The Carrion Grubs got into the larder at Crown Guard before we left, and now they're all along the road west. They eat everything that dies out there, and then they eat everything that's alive and slow. Kaia's lost every snare she's set this month, and I've lost a cart of turnips.

They swarm the road and the ditches beside it. They're slow and they're soft, but there are always more of them. Burn them if you can, because they don't like it.
plw_carrion_grubs.accept_text: Burn them if you can. They don't like it.

plw_cartmaster_corin.description:
Cartmaster Corin gave the crossing its name. He ran a carting business there before the plague, and now he runs it for the Cult, with the same ledgers and the same smile. I bought every horse in this stable off him, and he gave me a fair price.

Bram says you've cleared the square. I want Corin dead and his ledgers burned.

He's in the old counting house at the crossing. He doesn't fight fair and he'll call everything nearby to help him, so take friends with you.
plw_cartmaster_corin.accept_text: Throw the ledgers on the fire before you leave the counting house. I don't want them read.

plw_corins_crossing.description:
Corin's Crossing was a crossroads town when I was a boy. Fairs, horse sales, a pie shop I still think about. The Cult took it over, and now it's where the plague carts load.

The Cult Plaguebringers fill the barrels in the square, and the Cult Cart Drivers take them out to whatever farms are still alive. I've followed those carts. I've seen what's left after they leave.

The crossing's on the road west, where the roads cross. Kill the plaguebringers first, because they'll throw the barrels at you if you give them time.
plw_corins_crossing.accept_text: Stay clear of any broken barrel you see. What's in them soaks into the ground and stays.

plw_crow_pie.description:
I'm Greta, and I kept the beds at Crown Guard, and now I keep the chapel's kitchen, and the chapel eats better than it did, if I say so myself.

My grandmother made crow pie, and the Stead Crows at the Marris Stead are the fattest crows I've ever seen. They've been eating well. Don't think about what on.

They follow the farmhands at the stead, south of the road. Get the fat ones. And don't tell anyone what's in the pie until after they've had seconds.
plw_crow_pie.accept_text: Pluck them out there if you can stand to. I'd rather not have the feathers in my kitchen.

plw_gargoyles_over_the_gates.description:
I'm Gwen, and I flew Crown Guard's bats, and now I nurse the ones that come in hurt, and lately that's a lot of them.

The Gate Gargoyles over Stratholme have started coming out to meet the Dawn's bats on the western road. I lost two this month. The Stone-Winged Gargoyles that hunt the ground under them finish off whatever falls.

The gate ones roost on Stratholme's walls at the top of the road, and the wild ones hunt the open country below. Bring them down where you can reach them, because they don't like to land.
plw_gargoyles_over_the_gates.accept_text: Mind your head on the road. My riders say they come in low from behind.

plw_gargoyles_over_the_road.description:
Ser Roland Ashcombe. I keep the Dawn's watch on Stratholme, and the Stone-Winged Gargoyles keep watching me back.

They fly over the road out of the city and dive on anyone who looks at it too long. I've been looking at it too long for years.

They circle over the road north of Corin's Crossing, toward Stratholme. They'll turn to stone when they're hurt, so finish them quickly, and don't let them get above you.
plw_gargoyles_over_the_road.accept_text: Bring a heavy blade. A light one just chips the stone.

plw_gatekeeper_vorthas.description:
Gatekeeper Vorthas was a captain of Stratholme's guard. He held the gate when the city fell, and he holds it still, for the Scourge now. I served under him. He taught me how to hold a shield.

I'd like my old captain at rest. I can't do it myself. I've tried, and I couldn't lift my sword.

He stands at the gate, where he always stood. He's a death knight now, and he's strong. Take friends, and don't fight him alone.
plw_gatekeeper_vorthas.accept_text: If his shield falls, bring it back to me. I'll hang it in the chapel.

plw_hound_fangs.description:
I've run out of arrowheads. The Plague Hounds on the road west have fangs as hard as flint, and I've been knapping them into points. They fly true, truer than the steel ones.

The hounds run in packs along the road, past the old tower. Pull the big canines, the ones at the front. I'll do the rest by the fire.
plw_hound_fangs.accept_text: Pull them with pliers if you've got them. Twisting cracks the root.

plw_old_marris.description:
Old Marris was the head of the family. He built that farm with his own hands and he never let anyone forget it. He still walks it, still giving orders to the dead.

He was hard on me, the first summer. By the second, he'd taught me to plough. I'd like him to rest with the others.

He's in the farmhouse, or in the barn behind it. He's strong, because he always was. Take friends if you can, and be kind to him if you can't.
plw_old_marris.accept_text: Close the barn door behind you when it's done. He always hated it left open.

plw_plaguewood.description:
I'm Kaia, and I herded reindeer outside Tromso before the Integration, and now I hunt for the chapel. Plaguewood is the worst hunting ground I've ever seen.

The Plaguewood Spiders spin webs across every path, and the Plaguewood Crypt Fiends dig under them and come up through the floor. Nothing lives in there that I'd want to eat.

Plaguewood's north-west of Corin's Crossing, on the road to Stratholme. The spiders are in the trees and the fiends are underground. Watch where you step.
plw_plaguewood.accept_text: Burn a path through the webs as you go. It'll make the way back easier.

plw_plaguewood_silk.description:
I make my own snares, and the Plaguewood Spiders spin silk that's stronger than any rope in the Plaguelands. I'd like enough to rig snares round the whole chapel. The dead don't cross holy ground, but the animals do.

The spiders carry it in their glands. Cut it out carefully, because it sticks to everything, and wear gloves if you've got them.
plw_plaguewood_silk.accept_text: Roll it on a stick as you cut. If you ball it up, I'll never get it apart.

plw_sigils_of_the_fallen.description:
The Gate Death Knights still wear the sigils of the houses they served when they were alive. Barov, Mardenholde, and a dozen others. Ser Roland says the houses that are left don't know what became of their sons and daughters.

He'd like the sigils back, so he can tell them, and he's asked me to keep the tally while he watches the gate.

The death knights wear them on their breastplates. Cut them off and bring them to me. Ser Roland will know every house by its colours.
plw_sigils_of_the_fallen.accept_text: Keep them in separate pockets if you can. The colours rub off on each other.

plw_spore_caps.description:
The Spore-Walkers grow caps on their shoulders, and I think the caps are where the plague is changing. It's mixing with the fungus in there, and I need to see how. Nothing I learned on Earth covers this.

Cut the caps off the walkers in the vale. Put them in these sacks and tie them tight. If one starts to puff, drop it and don't look back. I can't stress that enough.
plw_spore_caps.accept_text: Hold the sacks away from you on the walk back. They'll swell a little, and that's normal.

plw_spores_for_the_sanctuary.description:
Dr. Sun's sealed a sample of the vale's spores in wax, and she's asked me to find somebody going south, because she's busy with the vale. There's a botanist at the Emerald Sanctuary in Felwood, Yuki Hashimoto, who's cataloguing everything that grows back in corrupted ground. If anyone's seen something like this, it's her.

The doctor would like her to compare it with what grows in Felwood.

Take the zeppelin from Tirisfal to Orgrimmar, then go north through Ashenvale to Felwood. Yuki's at the Sanctuary, probably on her knees in a flowerbed. Don't break the wax, and don't let a bat sit on it.
plw_spores_for_the_sanctuary.accept_text: Don't break the wax, and don't let a bat sit on it.

plw_terrordale.description:
I'm Osric Vey, the Dawn's gravewarden. We bury our own here, and anyone else who needs it. Terrordale is full of people nobody buried.

The Terrordale Ghouls hunt the valley floor and the Terrordale Spirits wail along the hills above them. I'd like the valley quieter before I take a spade to it.

Terrordale's in the south-west, past the Marris Stead. Stay out of the spirits' reach, because they'll drain you.
plw_terrordale.accept_text: Mark where the ghouls are thickest. That's where I'll start digging.

plw_the_baron.description:
I'm Jessa Moonfield, and I keep the beds here. I grew up in Stratholme. My mother baked for the Baron's household, and he tipped well at midwinter.

When the plague came he sold himself to the Lich King, and now the dead half of the city is his. Baron Rivendare rules it from the Slaughter Square at the back of Stratholme, where the Scourge stitch their abominations together. He rides out on a black horse some nights and looks up at this chapel, and he can't come any closer.

You'll have to bring down the ziggurats before you can reach him, and then you'll need a full company and a steady healer. Put him down. He was never a kind man, but he was ours.
plw_the_baron.accept_text: Come back and tell me when it's done. I'd like to stop watching for that horse.

plw_the_crossings_abominations.description:
The Cult's noticed its drivers are dying, and it's brought in muscle. There are Crossing Abominations standing in the square now, round the carts, and they don't move unless something comes close.

I'd like them brought down before the Cult finds another use for them.

They're slow and they hit like a falling barn. Pull them one at a time if you can, and keep the carts between you and the rest.
plw_the_crossings_abominations.accept_text: Check what's in the carts when they're down. I'd like to know what they've been guarding.

plw_the_family_crypt.description:
There's a crypt under the stead where the family's always buried its own. I've heard the dead down there don't stay in their niches any more.

The Crypt Shamblers walk the passages and the Marris Ossuary Guards stand at the doors. The guards were the family's own men once, and they'll still try to stop you.

The stair down's at the stead, south of the farmhouse. It's laid out like a grid down there, so count your turns. I'd like the family back where they were put.
plw_the_family_crypt.accept_text: Leave the doors open behind you when you come back up. They should have air.

plw_the_fungal_mass.description:
At the heart of the vale there's something I can only call a mass. A fungus the size of a house, that moves when it wants to. Everything else in the vale is feeding it, or it's feeding them. I can't tell which and I don't think it matters.

The Fungal Mass. Kill it, and the rest will start dying back.

It sits in the middle of the vale and it'll come at you when you get close. It's huge and it's poisonous. Take friends and take antidotes.
plw_the_fungal_mass.accept_text: Bring me a piece of it if you can carry one without touching it.

plw_the_fungal_vale.description:
I'm Dr. Sun Li. I studied fungi in Kunming for twenty years, back home, and the Fungal Vale is the most frightening thing I've ever seen.

Something is growing there, and it isn't one thing. The Vale Plague Slimes crawl along the ground spreading it, and the Spore-Walkers drift between the caps carrying it on their backs. Every week it's a little wider.

The vale's north of Corin's Crossing, on the road toward Stratholme. Thin them before it spreads further. Don't breathe the spores, and keep your mouth shut while you're in there. I mean that literally.
plw_the_fungal_vale.accept_text: Tie a cloth over your face before you go in. It won't stop everything, but it helps.

plw_the_gates_of_stratholme.description:
Stratholme's gate is held by Gate Death Knights, with Gate Gargoyles perched over them. I was a knight of Lordaeron before the city fell. Some of those death knights were my brothers in arms. I know their shields.

Thin the gate, so the Dawn can get close enough to see inside.

Follow the road north past the Fungal Vale and west through Plaguewood, and the gate's at the end of it. The death knights don't retreat, so pick them off one at a time.
plw_the_gates_of_stratholme.accept_text: If one of them falls with his visor up, look at his face for me. I might know him.

plw_the_gorger.description:
I'm a mycologist. I came through in the Integration and I study what the plague does to living things, because somebody has to, and the somebody turned out to be me.

The abominations in the Slaughter Square are stitched from whatever the Scourge drag in. The biggest one is Ramstein the Gorger, and he eats. He eats the dead and the living and the plague with them, and he carries more of it than anything else in the city.

Kill him before he walks out of that square. I've seen what's in him under a lens. Earth never had anything like it, and I'd like it to stay in Stratholme.
plw_the_gorger.accept_text: Don't let him get a hand on you. I've seen what he does with the ones he catches.

plw_the_grand_crusader.description:
I was a knight of Lordaeron before Stratholme fell. I stood outside its gate the morning the prince came, and I didn't go in. I've had a long time to think about that.

The Crusade holds the living half of the city now, the market and the halls. Grand Crusader Dathrohan commands it from the Hall of High Command, and he burns anyone he thinks might be carrying the plague, which is everyone he doesn't like.

Something about him is wrong. His own men won't meet his eyes. Go into the city and find out what he is, and then end him. Whatever he turns out to be.
plw_the_grand_crusader.accept_text: Watch his men when you face him. If they don't fight for him, you'll know I was right.

plw_the_manifest.description:
The drivers carry manifests. Every barrel, every farm, every day it's due. If I had one, the Dawn could warn those farms before the carts got there.

Find a Cult Cart Driver at the crossing and take his manifest off him. It'll be in his coat, inside pocket, because they're tidy people, the Cult. Bring it back as fast as you can. Those carts don't wait for anybody.
plw_the_manifest.accept_text: Don't stop to read it. Bring it straight back and I'll get riders out tonight.

plw_the_marris_locket.description:
My husband's sister wore a brass locket with a painting of the whole family inside. She wore it every day, even in the fields. She's still wearing it, out there with the others.

I'd like it back. I'd like something of theirs that isn't the farm.

She'll be one of the farmhands at the stead. It's a little brass locket on a chain. You'll know it when you see it.
plw_the_marris_locket.accept_text: If the chain breaks, bring the pieces. I can mend a chain.

plw_the_marris_stead.description:
I'm Edda Marris. I married into the family two summers before the plague, and I was in town the day it reached the farm. I came home and they were all still working. Mother, my husband, his sister, the hands, every one of them still working.

I came here so I didn't have to watch. I'm done not watching.

The Marris Stead is south of the road, toward Terrordale. The Marris Farmhands work the fields and the Stead Crows follow them, picking. They were good people. They'd want it quick.
plw_the_marris_stead.accept_text: Leave the plough where it stands. I'll see to that myself.

plw_the_plaguewood_matriarch.description:
Every spider in Plaguewood came out of the same nest, and the thing that laid them is still sitting on it. I call her the Plaguewood Matriarch. She's bigger than a horse.

As long as she's there, the wood fills up again as fast as we empty it.

She's in the deepest part of Plaguewood, where the webs are thickest. She's fast and she's poisonous. Take friends, and bring a knife for the webs.
plw_the_plaguewood_matriarch.accept_text: Burn the nest when she's down, or the wood will be full again by spring.

plw_the_road_west.description:
Bram Tolliver, outrider. I used to ride out of Crown Guard. Now I ride out of here, and it's a longer ride, and I'm still the only one who does it.

The road west runs past the old tower and over into the western half of the Plaguelands, all the way to the river. The Plague Hounds hunt along it in packs, and the Frenzied Ghouls come up out of the ditches the moment they hear a horse.

I'd like that road safe enough for somebody other than me. The hounds run the open ground and the ghouls wait in the ditches. Don't stop moving, because they'll swarm you if you do.
plw_the_road_west.accept_text: Keep moving, because they swarm anything that stands still.

plw_the_sexton.description:
Edda Marris came to the chapel about her family's crypt, and the chapel means me. The family's sexton buried every Marris for forty years, and he didn't stop when the plague came. Sexton Hollowell is still down there digging, and the dead he's buried sing for him. The Bone Choir, the farmhands called it, before they were in it.

She'd like him put in the ground for good, and the singing stopped. I'll say the words once you've done the rest.

His hall's in the middle of the crypt, and the choir sings from the chapel at the head of it. You'll hear them both. Don't listen to the words, because they'll tell you to lie down.
plw_the_sexton.accept_text: Stuff your ears with something if you can. It won't keep it all out, but it helps.

plw_the_skeletal_mages.description:
Terrordale's dead don't stay down, because the Terrordale Skeletal Mages raise them again every night. They were Kirin Tor once, I think, sent to fight the plague and lost to it. They still wear the violet.

I'd like them destroyed. Nobody can rest in that valley while they're standing.

They stand among the dead, raising them. Kill them quickly, because they'll raise anything you kill near them.
plw_the_skeletal_mages.accept_text: If any of them still carry their books, bring them. Somebody who knew the Kirin Tor might want them back.

plw_the_terror_of_the_dale.description:
Terrordale's named for what lives in it. The Terror of the Dale was a lich's apprentice who stayed behind when the lich went north, and it's held the valley ever since.

I'd like it ended, so the valley can be buried properly. I've been putting off the digging for a year.

It holds the ruined chapel in the middle of Terrordale. It's a caster, and it'll freeze you if you let it. Take friends, and keep moving.
plw_the_terror_of_the_dale.accept_text: Eat something warm before you go. You'll need the heat in you.

plw_the_three_ziggurats.description:
I fly over Stratholme most days, and from up there you can see what the ground can't. The Scourge raised three ziggurats in the dead half of the city, and each one has a keeper. Nerub'enkan is a spider lord out of the north. Baroness Anastari was a lady of the court and is a banshee now. Maleki the Pallid is a lich who keeps his ziggurat as cold as a tomb.

While those three stand, the Baron's gate stays shut. Osric buries what comes out of the city, and he'd like it to stop. Kill all three keepers and the way opens.

Go in from the service gate, where the Scourge bring their carts.
plw_the_three_ziggurats.accept_text: Rest between the three. Nobody's timing you.

plw_what_grew_in_the_jar.description:
I catalogue everything that grows back in Felwood, and somebody sent me a jar of spores from the Plaguelands' Fungal Vale. I put it on my bench a week ago. It's grown, and it's grown into something I've never seen.

Dr. Sun Li needs to see what her spores turn into. She's with the Argent Dawn at Light's Hope Chapel, at the far east end of the Eastern Plaguelands.

It's a long way, so wrap the jar in something and keep it upright. It's started tapping on the glass, and I'd rather it didn't get out.
plw_what_grew_in_the_jar.accept_text: If the lid starts to lift, put your hand on it and walk faster.

plw_word_for_sun_rock.description:
The Forsaken say the dead are rising in Mulgore, across the sea, with nobody calling them. There's a tauren spiritwalker at Sun Rock Retreat in Stonetalon, Tohana, trying to understand why.

I've written down everything I know about Terrordale. How the dead rose, how they stayed up, what put them down. It might help her. It might not. It's what I have.

Take the zeppelin from Tirisfal to Orgrimmar and a wind rider to Sun Rock. Tohana's the spiritwalker by the fire. Give it to her and nobody else.
plw_word_for_sun_rock.accept_text: Wait while she reads it, if she'll let you. I'd like to know what she makes of it.
